title: an alias takes the standing of its record
line: the name as written on a record accepted for a person is an alias with that record's standing, and the rule stands on the accepted ones alone: Helen Sara Brant's memorial, whose identity the rule takes, leaves its words for her, Helen Sara Brant Ahearn, an undecided alias the matcher reads and the rule does not; her christening, taken by the rule, leaves Helen Sarah Brandt an accepted alias the rule counts; the rule's decision withdrawn, that alias is undecided again and counts no more

steps.say: her names before any record: the name the file gives, nothing more
her memorial arrives, the page the owner saved, and the rule takes her identity on it
the memorial's words for her are an alias of a page anyone can edit: undecided, read by the matcher, never by the rule

expect.why: a page anyone can edit identifies a person and builds none of their facts, the name it writes among them
the rule stands on the accepted name and accepted aliases alone; the matcher's search still reads the page's words

steps.say: her own christening, a record nobody can edit at will, taken by the rule

expect.why: the christening's words for her take its standing: accepted
the rule counts an accepted alias as her name

steps.say: the rule takes its decision on the christening back

expect.why: the alias goes back to undecided with the statements the decision wrote
a decision taken back no longer shapes the rule's later ones
